pages.title: Atlas Q2 Plan
pages.body:
Owner: Lena Fischer (Product). Engineering lead: Priya Raman. Last planning review: 2026-04-02.

## Goal

Replace the legacy subscription biller with metered usage billing, refunds, and chargebacks, and launch the new billing platform on **2026-06-30**.

## Workstreams

1. Metered usage billing engine — Priya Raman
2. Refunds: integration, reconciliation, and the support-agent refund API — Priya Raman and Aisha Okonkwo
3. Chargebacks: webhook receiver and dispute handling — Diego Santos
4. Customer-facing billing portal — Diego Santos
5. Migration of legacy subscriptions — Priya Raman

## Payments vendor

We are building refunds and chargebacks on **Nordwind Payments**, selected in March 2026 over two other bidders on settlement coverage and on their published v3 API. The contract commits Nordwind to sandbox parity with production for every v3 endpoint we depend on.

The pieces of Nordwind we depend on:

- v3 refunds API, plus a sandbox we can certify against before go-live
- v3 webhook delivery, including the signature-verification specification for the chargeback receiver
- Settlement files in the sandbox, which the nightly reconciliation job parses

### Nordwind contacts

- **Ines Brandt** — Partner Success Manager, ines.brandt@nordwindpayments.example. She is our named escalation route and she sends delivery and delay notices **by email**, not through the partner portal.
- Developer relations — devrel@nordwindpayments.example, for specification questions.

> Anything Nordwind tells us arrives in email. It does not appear in the partner portal and it does not land on a Jira ticket unless one of us copies it there by hand. If a ticket says we are waiting on the vendor and does not say why, the reason is in the mail.

## Key dates as planned in April

- Nordwind v3 refunds sandbox available: 2026-05-29
- Refunds integration certified: 2026-06-15
- Chargeback webhook receiver live: 2026-06-19
- Launch readiness review: 2026-06-24
- **Launch: 2026-06-30**

## Risks recorded at planning time

- Nordwind sandbox parity is contractual but unproven; every refunds workstream is downstream of it.
- The v3 webhook signing specification was still unpublished at planning time. We assumed the v2 document would carry over.
- Beacon's v2 event envelope has to be frozen before our usage-event schema can align to it.

## Dependencies on other teams

- Beacon — the usage event schema alignment cannot finish until Beacon freezes the v2 event envelope. See the Beacon Roadmap H2 2026 page.
- Comet — in-app plan management needs the billing portal endpoints, so Comet follows our launch date rather than setting its own.

pages.title: Beacon Roadmap H2 2026
pages.body:
Owner: Grace Lin (Product). Engineering lead: Tomas Ferreira.

## Themes

1. Identity resolution rewrite — Nadia Haddad
2. Freeze the v2 event envelope — Tomas Ferreira
3. Warehouse export connectors — Ravi Iyer

## Sequencing

The envelope freeze cannot happen before the identity resolution rewrite lands, because the rewrite changes which identifier is canonical on every event. Freezing first would mean freezing the wrong shape and re-cutting it a month later.

- Identity resolution rewrite — completed 2026-06-26
- v2 event envelope frozen — completed 2026-07-03

## Who is waiting on us

Atlas cannot align its usage event schema until the envelope is frozen. That was the only Atlas item ever blocked on another **internal** team rather than on a vendor, and it cleared on 2026-07-03.

> Worth stating plainly, because the two get conflated in status meetings: the Atlas refunds work was never blocked on Beacon. It was blocked on the payments vendor.

pages.title: Atlas Launch Retro (draft)
pages.body:
Draft, written 2026-08-17 by Marcus Whitfield. Not yet reviewed with the team.

## What happened

We planned to launch on 2026-06-30 and launched on **2026-08-14**, six weeks late.

The cause was single and external: Nordwind Payments did not deliver the v3 refunds sandbox on the date they committed to. Everything else followed from that. Refunds could not be certified, reconciliation had no settlement files to parse, the support-agent refund API had nothing to call, and the launch readiness review came back no-go on 2026-06-24 with refunds and chargebacks both blocked.

The chargeback receiver was blocked separately and for a related reason: the v3 webhook signature-verification specification did not exist when we needed it. We had assumed the v2 signing document carried over. It did not — the header name and the canonicalisation both changed.

## Decision to move the launch

Marcus Whitfield recommended moving the launch to 2026-08-14 on 2026-06-11, on the grounds that a biller which cannot process a refund is not launchable. Fatima Al-Rashid approved it the following day. Lena Fischer announced the revised date to the team on 2026-06-15.

## What went wrong in how we tracked it

- Nordwind's delay notice arrived **by email** on 2026-06-08 and was never linked to a ticket. The refunds ticket said "blocked on the provider" for two months without ever naming Nordwind or quoting what they actually said.
- Anyone reading only Jira could see that four issues were blocked and that a date moved twice. They could not see why, who told us, or when.

## Actions

- [ ] Mirror every vendor delivery or delay notice into the blocked ticket, quoting the message and its date — Lena Fischer
- [ ] Name the vendor in the ticket, not just "the provider" — Lena Fischer
- [x] Record Nordwind's escalation contact in the Q2 plan — Lena Fischer
- [ ] Ask Nordwind for a contractual notice period on sandbox slips — Marcus Whitfield

pages.title: Atlas <> Nordwind sync — 2026-06-10
pages.body:
Attendees: Priya Raman, Marcus Whitfield, Lena Fischer, Ines Brandt (Nordwind Payments).

Called at two days' notice after Nordwind's delay notice of 2026-06-08.

## Notes

- Ines confirmed the v3 refunds sandbox has slipped and that Nordwind will not commit to a date beyond "late July". The cause on their side is a settlement-ledger migration that overran.
- Priya restated that our contract tests pass against our own mock and that certification is the only thing outstanding. There is no engineering work left on our side to bring forward.
- Marcus asked whether a partial sandbox — refunds without settlement files — could be made available sooner. Ines would not commit.
- Diego's request for the v3 webhook signature-verification specification was raised again. Ines confirmed it is written but unpublished and could not give a date.

## Consequences agreed in the room

- The 2026-06-30 launch is not achievable. Marcus to take a revised date to Fatima Al-Rashid.
- Refunds-dependent issues stay blocked rather than being reassigned; there is no work to move to.

## Actions

- [x] Marcus to recommend a revised launch date — done 2026-06-11
- [x] Ines to escalate the webhook signing specification internally
- [ ] Priya to re-run certification within 48 hours of the sandbox becoming available

pages.title: Comet Release Checklist
pages.body:
Owner: Oskar Nowak. Applies to every Comet mobile release.

## Before submitting a build

- [x] Crash-free sessions above 99.5% on the previous build
- [x] TestFlight soak of at least 48 hours
- [ ] Screenshots refreshed for any changed screen
- [ ] Release notes reviewed by Grace Lin

## Known holds

In-app plan management is built against a mock and cannot ship until Atlas exposes the plan-change endpoint, which sits behind the Atlas billing portal work. Comet is planning for September rather than tracking the Atlas launch date directly.

## Store submission

1. Tag the release branch
2. Upload from CI, never from a laptop
3. Submit for review by Tuesday to land in the same week
